claims.text: Drowzee uses a logic-programming-aided metamorphic testing technique to detect fact-conflicting hallucinations in large language models.
Tested LLMs exhibit hallucination rates ranging from 24.7% to 59.8% across nine domains.
Large language models struggle with temporal concepts.
Large language models struggle with out-of-distribution knowledge.
Large language models lack logical reasoning capabilities in hallucination detection contexts.
Model editing techniques are effective for mitigating fact-conflicting hallucinations on a small scale of fewer than 1000 knowledge pieces.

evidence.description: Evaluation of six LLMs across nine domains yielded measured hallucination rates between 24.7% and 59.8%.
Model editing techniques were evaluated and shown effective when applied to fewer than 1000 knowledge pieces.

methodologies.name: Drowzee Metamorphic Testing Framework
methodologies.description: A logic-programming-aided metamorphic testing framework that constructs a factual knowledge base, transforms knowledge using logical reasoning rules into test cases, and evaluates LLM reasoning via semantic-aware oracles.

limitations.text: Existing FCH detection relies on manually curated static benchmarks that fail to cover evolving FCH cases.
Validating reasoning behind LLM outputs is inherently difficult, particularly for complex logical relations.
Model editing mitigation was only demonstrated to be effective on a small scale involving fewer than 1000 knowledge pieces.

future_work.text: Continued community efforts to detect and mitigate model hallucinations.
